content.title: About
content.content: Baby Toddler peas, Stage 1 are gently cooked, fully pureed pea bites designed for infants aged 6–12 months. Made from 100 % whole peas with no added sugar, salt, or artificial flavors.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peas are one of the first vegetables introduced to a baby’s diet because of their mild flavor and soft texture.
Stage 1 means a completely smooth consistency with no visible pieces, reducing choking risk.
Peas are rich in plant protein and iron, important for a child’s growth and development.
The product is packaged in airtight single‑serve pouches, convenient for travel and storage.
It contains no gluten, dairy, or nuts, making it hypoallergenic.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Peas provide about 5 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle tissue growth in infants.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Iron from peas helps form hemoglobin and prevents anemia.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains folate, thiamine, and vitamin B6, which are vital for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Supports healthy gut microbiota and aids digestion.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Suitable for baby nutrition where salt intake should be limited.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some infants may be allergic to peas; monitor for any reaction when first introduced.

items.title: Over‑feeding
items.content: Large amounts can cause gas and abdominal discomfort.

items.title: Storage after opening
items.content: Once the pouch is opened, keep it refrigerated and use within 24 hours.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve a spoonful of the smooth puree using a baby‑friendly spoon. It can be mixed with breast milk, formula, or fruit puree for flavor variety.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened pouches in a cool, dry place at up to 25 °C. After opening, refrigerate and consume within 24 hours. Discard if an off‑odor or color change occurs.

chicken-or-turkey-garden-salad-with-chee.title: Garden Salad with Chicken or Turkey, Cheese, Lettuce and Vegetables, No Dressing

content.title: About
content.content: The garden salad combines cooked or roasted chicken and/or turkey breast, mild cheese, lettuce or mixed greens, tomatoes and/or carrots, and other fresh vegetables. It is served without dressing, allowing the natural flavors of the ingredients to shine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey are lean sources of high‑quality protein that are easily digested.
Cheese adds calcium and a creamy texture to the salad.
Leafy greens provide vitamins A, C, K and folate.
Tomatoes contain lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that is even more bioavailable when cooked, but still beneficial fresh.
The lack of dressing makes the dish low‑calorie and suitable for diet plans.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey supply essential amino acids needed for muscle maintenance and tissue repair.

items.title: Bone support
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium and phosphorus, important for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Tomatoes and carrots are high in beta‑carotene and lycopene, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Immune system boost
items.content: Vitamin C from tomatoes and greens enhances the body’s immune response.

items.title: Low in unhealthy fats
items.content: Without dressing and using lean meat, the salad is low in saturated fat, supporting heart health.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improperly cooked or stored chicken/turkey can harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Some cheeses are salty, which should be considered by those limiting sodium intake.

items.title: Nutrient interactions
items.content: Large amounts of cheese can inhibit iron absorption from leafy greens.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled. It can be enjoyed as a standalone meal or as a side dish. If desired, add a light drizzle of lemon juice or balsamic vinegar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, store protein, cheese, and vegetables separately to prevent the leaves from becoming soggy.

chocolate-milk-reduced-sugar-reduced-fat.title: Chocolate Milk, Reduced Sugar, Reduced Fat (2%)

content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate milk with reduced sugar and reduced fat (2%) is a beverage made from skimmed cow’s milk, enriched with cocoa butter and natural flavorings. The lower sugar content makes it more suitable for people monitoring glucose levels, while the reduced fat percentage keeps a creamy texture with fewer calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sugar is reduced to about 5 g per 250 ml, making it roughly half as sweet as regular chocolate milk.
Cocoa butter used in the formulation retains some of the polyphenols found in dark chocolate.
Skimmed milk preserves a high level of calcium and vitamin D, essential for bone health.
The drink is often used in sports nutrition as a quick source of carbs and protein after workouts.
In some countries the product is certified as “low‑calorie” and sold in a dedicated diet‑food aisle.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Skimmed milk provides over 300 mg of calcium per 250 ml, supporting strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Each serving delivers about 8 g of milk protein, aiding muscle recovery.

items.title: Reduced sugar
items.content: Lower sugar helps control blood glucose spikes and reduces the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Contains polyphenols
items.content: Cocoa butter contributes antioxidant polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Milk supplies riboflavin (B2) and vitamin B12, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The product contains lactose; those with intolerance should choose lactose‑free alternatives.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein or whey may experience reactions.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: Some versions may contain trace amounts of caffeine from cocoa; caffeine‑sensitive persons should be aware.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Flavor enhancers and stabilizers may be added; check the label if you are sensitive to food additives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chocolate milk can be enjoyed cold as a refreshing drink, blended into smoothies, added to oatmeal or protein shakes. It can be gently warmed, but avoid boiling to preserve flavor and texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 1–4 °C. After opening, consume within 5–7 days. Do not freeze, as this may cause separation and texture changes.

stuffed-shells-with-fish-and-or-shellfis.title: Stuffed shells with fish and/or shellfish in tomato sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Stuffed shells (conchiglioni) are large pasta “pockets” filled with a mixture of fish, shellfish and sometimes cheese, baked in a fragrant tomato sauce. The dish is popular in Mediterranean cuisine and is often served as a first course or a light main.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional fillings use white fish such as cod or sea bass together with shellfish like shrimp, mussels or calamari.
The tomato sauce is usually seasoned with basil, oregano and olive oil, which accentuates the sea flavors.
In Italy a similar dish is called “conchiglioni ripieni” and is served on festive occasions.
Stuffed shells can be assembled ahead of time, frozen, and baked whenever needed.
The dish is rich in protein and omega‑3 fatty acids when fish and shellfish are included.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Fish and shellfish provide complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Found in fatty fish and many shellfish, they support heart health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Includes B12, B6 and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Lycopene in tomato sauce
items.content: Lycopene is a powerful antioxidant that helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Minerals (iodine, zinc, selenium)
items.content: Shellfish are good sources of these trace elements, vital for immune function and hormone balance.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to fish, shrimp, mussels or other seafood.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce and seafood can be high in salt; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improper storage of fish and shellfish can lead to bacterial growth and food poisoning.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: Certain fish may contain mercury or other heavy metals; choose reputable sources.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Serve hot, sprinkled with fresh parsley or basil and grated Parmesan. It pairs well with a light green salad, garlic bread, or creamy polenta.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked stuffed shells in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days in an airtight container. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 3 months. Reheat thoroughly to ensure safety.

content.title: About
content.content: Whole wheat bread is bread made from flour that contains all parts of the wheat kernel: the bran, the germ, and the endosperm. It is darker, denser, and nuttier in flavor than white bread. Whole wheat bread is eaten as sandwiches, toast, and alongside meals, and it is a common source of whole grains in the diet.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole wheat flour keeps the bran and germ that are removed when white flour is made.
Bread labeled simply as wheat bread is not always whole grain, so check that whole wheat flour is the first ingredient.
Whole wheat bread is usually denser and has a stronger, nuttier flavor than white bread.
Whole grains such as whole wheat have been a staple food for thousands of years.
Sourdough fermentation can also be used to make whole wheat bread.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Whole wheat bread contains more fiber than white bread, which supports digestion and fullness.

items.title: Contains B vitamins
items.content: Whole wheat bread provides niacin, thiamin, and folate, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Whole wheat bread contains magnesium, selenium, iron, and zinc.

items.title: Slower-digesting carbohydrates
items.content: Whole grain bread generally raises blood sugar more slowly than white bread.

items.title: Part of a whole-grain diet
items.content: Eating whole grains is associated with better overall diet quality.

items.title: Gluten and wheat allergy
items.content: Whole wheat bread contains gluten and should be avoided by people with celiac disease, gluten sensitivity, or wheat allergy.

items.title: Sodium and added sugar
items.content: Some commercial breads contain a lot of salt and added sugar, so check labels.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Fiber and fructans in wheat may cause gas or bloating in sensitive individuals, including people with irritable bowel syndrome.

items.title: Misleading labels
items.content: Some breads are colored to look whole wheat but are made mostly from refined flour. Look for whole wheat flour as the first ingredient.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Whole wheat bread can be eaten as toast, sandwiches, bruschetta, or with soups, salads, and spreads. Pair it with protein and vegetables for a balanced meal. Choose breads with whole wheat flour as the first ingredient and lower sodium and sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store whole wheat bread at room temperature in a bread box or a closed bag for two to four days. For longer storage, slice and freeze it, then toast slices straight from the freezer. Refrigeration can dry it out faster. Discard bread that shows any mold.
